text: Sequence transduction, such as machine translation, has been dominated by recurrent neural networks that map an input sequence to a variable length output sequence.

citations.quote: The prevalent approach to sequence to sequence learning maps an input sequence to a variable length output sequence via recurrent neural networks.

text: Neural machine translation trains a single network jointly to maximize translation performance.

citations.quote: Unlike the traditional statistical machine translation, the neural machine translation aims at building a single neural network that can be jointly tuned to maximize the translation performance.

text: Recurrent computation is sequential along the sequence, which limits parallelization within training examples as sentences get longer.
Recurrent translation models differ mainly in how the decoder reads the source sentence.

citations.quote: Unlike the traditional statistical machine translation, the neural machine translation aims at building a single neural network that can be jointly tuned to maximize the translation performance.

text: Basic encoder-decoders compress a source sentence into a fixed-length vector from which the decoder generates a translation, whereas Bahdanau et al. let the model soft-search for the parts of the source sentence that are relevant to predicting a target word.

citations.quote: The models proposed recently for neural machine translation often belong to a family of encoder-decoders and consists of an encoder that encodes a source sentence into a fixed-length vector from which a decoder generates a translation.

In this paper, we conjecture that the use of a fixed-length vector is a bottleneck in improving the performance of this basic encoder-decoder architecture, and propose to extend this by allowing a model to automatically (soft-)search for parts of a source sentence that are relevant to predicting a target word, without having to form these parts as a hard segment explicitly.

text: Both variants keep long short-term memory style recurrence and therefore process tokens one step at a time.
Convolutional models trade recurrence for parallelism: compared to recurrent models, computations over all elements can be fully parallelized during training.

citations.quote: Compared to recurrent models, computations over all elements can be fully parallelized during training and optimization is easier since the number of non-linearities is fixed and independent of the input length.

text: Deep convolutional stacks rely on residual learning to remain trainable.

citations.quote: We present a residual learning framework to ease the training of networks that are substantially deeper than those used previously.

text: In contrast to attention over all positions, a convolution only relates positions within its kernel, so distant positions are connected through several layers.

Thus recurrent models compute sequentially and convolutional models need several layers to connect distant positions: no existing transduction model is both fully parallel and connects any two positions in a constant number of operations.

text: We propose the Transformer, an encoder-decoder based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions.
On WMT 2014 English-to-German the Transformer reaches 28.4 BLEU, more than 2 BLEU above the best previous results including ensembles.
We show that the Transformer generalizes to English constituency parsing with large and limited training data.
